findings.statement: US unemployment rate (FRED UNRATE): 14.8% in 2020-04 (the 2020 peak), vs a 2018 average of 3.9% (+10.9 pts)
Initial jobless claims (FRED ICSA) (level): 219,454 average in 2018; reached 4,663,250 in the 12 months to 2020-04; best correlation with the target r=+0.99 at a 1-month lead
Total nonfarm payrolls, YoY (FRED PAYEMS) (YoY change): 1.6% average in 2018; reached -13.4% in the 12 months to 2020-04; best correlation with the target r=-0.97 at a 0-month lead
Leisure & hospitality employment, YoY (FRED USLAH) (YoY change): 1.5% average in 2018; reached -47.2% in the 12 months to 2020-04; best correlation with the target r=-0.97 at a 0-month lead
Industrial production, YoY (FRED INDPRO) (YoY change): 3.2% average in 2018; reached -17.3% in the 12 months to 2020-04; best correlation with the target r=-0.76 at a 0-month lead
Federal funds rate (FRED FEDFUNDS) (level): 1.8% average in 2018; 0.1% at 2020-04; best correlation with the target r=+0.07 at a 9-month lead

answer.summary: US unemployment rose in 2020: 3.9 -> 14.8 (+10.9 pts, peak 2020-04). The evidence points mainly to (1) mass layoffs (initial jobless claims exploded); (2) shutdowns hit leisure & hospitality hardest; (3) industrial output fell.
